title: Wungram Okthot: The Novel of Highland Heritage and Clan Trials
alternate_titles: Wungram: A Chronicle of Tangkhul Highland Life
Heritage, Clan Kinship, and the Mountain Destiny
subject: Novel (Upanyas), Ethnohistory & Cultural Heritage
notes: Immersive cultural novel capturing 19th-century Tangkhul life: head-taking traditions giving way to peace treaties, clan genealogies, traditional feasts of merit (Maron), and ancestral wisdom.

front_matter.title_page: Wungram Okthot: The Novel of Highland Heritage and Clan Trials (1998)
front_matter.preface: Wungram Okthot weaves ethnohistorical authenticity with powerful novelistic storytelling. It preserves traditional terminology for ancient rituals, clan feasts of merit (Maron), wood-carving on village gates (Kharashim), and the philosophical foundations of Tangkhul identity.

chapters.title: The Feast of Merit (Maron Kasa)
chapters.summary: Depicts an elder staging the grand feast of merit, erecting sacrificial monoliths, and distributing meat to all clans.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Wungram elder akhana Maron (Feast of Merit) sakhavai ningkashang leisai. Maron kasana village-li saphā-kashang khangam machitheila, awui lungkashung eina mikumo pupupli kachak kala khor milaga village unity ngashankhavai leisai. Ana cattle thakharā shaksarlaga shang pupupli ngashanserie. Kala awui shim-ngalemli lungphung monolith akha kakor-hamsangie.
chapters.english_translation: An elder of Wungram resolved to perform the solemn Feast of Merit (Maron). This feast was intended not for vain ostentation, but to generously distribute cattle meat and rice brew to every clan, thereby cementing the spiritual and social unity of the village. He slaughtered cattle and distributed portions to all clans, and erected a memorial monolith beside his homestead.

vocabulary.meaning: feast of merit, traditional philanthropic festival

grammar_notes: Philanthropic motive clauses: redistributive economic structure.
exercises: What was the social purpose of the Feast of Merit in Tangkhul tradition?
Identify the structural components of the feast.

chapters.title: The Carving of the Village Gate (Kharashim Tarung)
chapters.summary: Master woodcarvers adorn the sacred village entrance gate with horned mithun emblems and sun symbols.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: Village-wui gate (Kharashim) kathara sakhavai, thing-artisanbingna Tarung kashang thingphun khuilaga village-li phung-ungserie. Athumna mithun (siel) horn, kazing-sira, kala warriors-wui emblem kaphāmei khak-saye. Kharashim china village-li kashikashili eina huikhuikhavai sacred barrier thada kasaye.
chapters.english_translation: To renew the village gateway (Kharashim), master artisans carried the sacred Tarung timber from the virgin forest. With adzes and chisels, they carved motifs of mithun horns, celestial stars, and brave warriors. The consecrated gate served as both a physical fortification and a spiritual shield safeguarding the village from evil.

vocabulary.meaning: mithun horn motif symbolizing wealth and fertility

chapters.title: The Covenant of the Four Mountain Villages
chapters.summary: Four historically warring mountain settlements establish a permanent peace pact and intermarriage alliance.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: Kaphung matiwui village-bingna ngaburlaga peace treaty sakahaisai. Athumna haikaphā salaga: 'Ithui yaronaobingna warfare kashikahailaga luiramli ot sara; ithui ngalanaobingna inter-marriage eina shangli unity phungsara.' Wungram kaphung tharili peace-wui mayāngwon shokserie.
chapters.english_translation: The four mountain villages assembled and consecrated a permanent peace pact. They solemnly pledged: 'Our youth shall cast aside war and till the terraced fields; our daughters shall unite the clans through honorable intermarriage.' And over the heights of Wungram, the rainbow of enduring peace shone bright.
grammar_notes: Treaty resolution parallelism: youths till fields; maidens unite clans through marriage.
exercises: Summarize the terms of the peace pact.
